plan.title: [framework-gap] check --no-suite hardcodes origin master, so the merge-chokepoint gate cannot run in a repo whose default branch is main

narratives.Description: `deft check --no-suite` fetched `origin master` with a constant refspec before any gate, so in a repo whose branch is `main` it exited 2, ran no gate, and blamed the network (#6970). This story makes the no-suite prep step resolve the delivery and comparison branches with the existing resolvers, bootstrap `origin/HEAD` from the remote only when nothing local names a default, fetch the comparison and delivery branches through the safe fetch helper, and tell a missing branch apart from other fetch failures with a source-matched fix.
narratives.Overview:
1. Resolve. `prepareNoSuiteRun` calls `resolveDeliveryBranch` and `resolveBaseBranch` with a `GitRunner` adapted from the `NoSuiteGitFn` seam (tests stay offline). Before any fetch it exits 2 (no gate) when a present policy value is malformed: `resolveDeliveryBranch` source `typed` with an error or source `default-on-error` names `plan.policy.deliveryBranch`; `resolveBaseBranch` source `typed` with an error or source `default-on-error` names `plan.policy.baseBranch`. The message carries the resolver's error text. A missing PROJECT-DEFINITION or a missing policy key is not malformed and does not refuse.
2. Remote default. When `resolveDeliveryBranch` returns source `default-fallback` (no `origin/HEAD`, no remote-tracking or local `main`/`master`), prep runs `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` and takes `<b>` from its `ref: refs/heads/<b>` line. When `<b>` passes `trackingFetchArgv`'s name check, prep fetches it with `trackingFetchArgv("origin", <b>)`, and only after that fetch succeeds runs `git remote set-head origin <b>` (which writes only `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`), then resolves both branches again, so the gates that find the default through `origin/HEAD` see the same branch. If the query, the name check, the fetch or `set-head` fails, prep keeps the fallback and goes on (item 5 then reports a missing fallback branch).
3. Fetch set. Comparison branch: the open PR's base ref when the head has exactly one open PR, else `resolveBaseBranch().branch`. Prep fetches the comparison branch, then the delivery branch when it differs (a branch already fetched in item 2 is not fetched twice), each with `trackingFetchArgv("origin", branch)`. A branch that fails `trackingFetchArgv`'s name check (including a PR base) exits 2 with the helper's error. The merge base is computed against `origin/<comparison branch>`; the no-PR fallback is never the literal `"master"`.
4. Provenance. Each fetched branch carries its source: `plan.policy.baseBranch`, `plan.policy.deliveryBranch`, `pull request #N base`, `origin/HEAD or an existing main/master ref`, `origin's HEAD branch`, or `framework fallback`. The header names each fetched branch with its source.
5. Failed fetch. Prep runs `git ls-remote --exit-code origin refs/heads/<branch>`. Exit 2: "check --no-suite: origin has no branch <b> (from <source>); no gate ran." plus a fix that matches the source: the policy key to correct for a configured branch; "retarget pull request #N or push its base branch" for a PR base; "set plan.policy.deliveryBranch (and plan.policy.baseBranch if pull requests merge into another branch)" for an inferred or fallback branch. Exit 0: "git fetch of <b> failed although origin has that branch" with git's stderr, and no network claim. Any other probe result: today's text (git's stderr plus "Restore network or remote access, then run again.").
6. Remove `NO_SUITE_MASTER_REFSPEC` from `no-suite.ts` and `check/index.ts`; the module doc says step 1 fetches the resolved branches.
7. One PR. Files: `packages/core/src/check/no-suite.ts`, `no-suite.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/check/index.ts`, one `changelog.d/` fragment. No change to the shared resolvers, no new verb, flag, constant or policy field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a repo whose `origin/HEAD` names `main` and no typed branch policy, when `check --no-suite` runs with no open PR, then it fetches `refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, computes the merge base against `origin/main`, never fetches `master`, and the header names `main`.
- Given typed `plan.policy.baseBranch` `develop` and typed `plan.policy.deliveryBranch` `main`, when `check --no-suite` runs with no open PR, then it fetches both `develop` and `main` and computes the merge base against `origin/develop`.
- Given one open PR whose base is `release`, when `check --no-suite` runs, then it fetches `release` and the delivery branch, and the merge base is against `origin/release`.
- Given no `origin/HEAD`, no `main`/`master` ref and no `origin/trunk` ref, and origin's HEAD branch is `trunk`, when `check --no-suite` runs, then it fetches `trunk` before running `git remote set-head origin trunk`, resolves the delivery branch to `trunk` afterwards, computes the merge base against `origin/trunk`, and never fetches `master`.
- Given the same repo but `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` fails, then prep does not run `set-head` and goes on with the fallback branch.
- Given the fetch of `main` fails and `git ls-remote --exit-code origin refs/heads/main` exits 2, then the command exits 2, runs no gate, and the message names `main`, its source, and the matching policy key or fix, and does not mention network access.
- Given the fetch fails and the probe exits 0, then the message keeps git's stderr and does not mention network access.
- Given the fetch fails and the probe fails for another reason, then the message is today's network text.
- Given `plan.policy.baseBranch` is `42`, `""`, or `bad:ref`, or `plan.policy.deliveryBranch` is `bad:ref` with no `baseBranch`, then the command exits 2 before any fetch and names the key.
- Given this repo (`origin/HEAD` names `master`), then it fetches only `master` as today.
narratives.Constraint:
- Fetching only the integration branch when the delivery branch differs (comment 7073397803 finding 1).
- A remote default found only inside prep that the gates cannot see (finding 2).
- Running `git remote set-head origin --auto`, or setting `origin/HEAD`, before the default branch's tracking ref exists (comment 7073432011 finding 1).
- Detecting a malformed policy value by an empty branch string alone (comment 7073397803 finding 3).
- A missing-branch probe by a short pattern, or calling a fetch failure a network problem when origin has the branch (finding 4).
- A remediation that names `plan.policy.baseBranch` for every source, or labels every inferred branch "origin HEAD" (finding 5).
- Matching git's localized stderr text; changing the shared resolvers or any gate's branch choice in this PR.
narratives.UserStory: As a consumer whose default branch is not master, I want `deft check --no-suite` to fetch the branch my project actually uses and to name a missing branch and its policy key, so that the merge-chokepoint gate runs before my PR instead of failing with a network message.

## In plain English
`deft check --no-suite` runs the merge-gate list before a PR, the way CI's merge-gate job does. Its first step is a fetch of `origin master`, with the refspec as a constant. In a repo whose default branch is `main` (the #6970 consumer also set `plan.policy.baseBranch` to `main`), that fetch fails, the command exits 2 and no gate runs. The message then says "Restore network or remote access", which is wrong: the network was fine, the branch does not exist. The consumer's PR merged without the gate.

Directive already has branch resolvers: `resolveBaseBranch` (typed `plan.policy.baseBranch`, else the delivery branch) and `resolveDeliveryBranch` (typed `plan.policy.deliveryBranch`, else `origin/HEAD`, else an existing `origin/main` or `origin/master`, else local `main` or `master`, else `master`). It also has a safe fetch argv helper, `trackingFetchArgv`. The no-suite path uses none of them.

The recommended fix: `check --no-suite` resolves the branch with those resolvers, fetches it with the safe helper, uses it as the merge-base fallback and in the header, and, when the fetch fails because origin has no such branch, says so, naming the branch and the policy key. One PR, no new verb, flag or policy field.

## Operator direction (Scott, 2026-11-21; relayed by the coordinator; recorded as constraints)
- Arc, then build through merge.
- Keep scope to `check --no-suite` unless a fix is trivially shared.

## Pains
- P1 — In a repo whose delivery or integration branch is not `master`, `check --no-suite` fetches `master`, exits 2 and runs no gate, so the merge-chokepoint gate cannot run before a PR (#6970).
- P2 — When the fetch fails because origin has no such branch, the message blames network or remote access instead of naming the missing branch and the policy key that would fix it (#6970).

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- Other `check --no-suite` output issues: #6827 (the "starting suite gate" line and three unrelated CLI items).
- Which branch each gate inside `check:merge` reads on its own; this arc changes only the no-suite preparation step.
- Directive's own CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) and release scripts that name `origin/master` for this repo.
- #3547 (closed; the earlier base-branch hardcode in finalize-cohort), cited only as precedent.

## Evidence
- #6970 (consumer, runtime 0.130.2, Windows, default branch `main`, `plan.policy.baseBranch` `main`): `check --no-suite: git fetch origin master:refs/remotes/origin/master failed (exit 128): fatal: couldn't find remote ref master; no gate ran. Restore network or remote access, then run again.`

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/check/no-suite.ts` 1-17 (module doc: step 1 fetches `origin master`). 30 `NO_SUITE_MASTER_REFSPEC`. 90-101 `defaultGit` (returns status, stdout, stderr). 187-197 `fetchFailure` (one message for every fetch failure, network text). 244-302 `prepareNoSuiteRun`: 250-253 the constant fetch; 259-267 the PR base ref (falls back to `"master"`, fetched only when not `master`); 269 merge base against `origin/<baseRef>`; 271-274 header "fetched origin/master".
- `packages/core/src/check/orchestrator.ts` 86-110: a failed prep prints its message and returns exit 2 before any gate.
- `packages/core/src/check/index.ts` 95: re-exports `NO_SUITE_MASTER_REFSPEC`; its only other user is `no-suite.test.ts` (18, 154-155, 188, 645).
- `packages/core/src/policy/delivery-branch.ts` 16 `FIELD_DELIVERY_BRANCH`; 20 `DEFAULT_DELIVERY_BRANCH_FALLBACK`; 22-26 sources (`typed`, `git-default`, `default-fallback`, `default-on-error`); 105-110 `assertSafeBranchName`; 127-149 `trackingFetchArgv` (`fetch origin -- refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/origin/<b>`); 176-213 `defaultBranchCandidates` (`symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, then remote-tracking, then local `main`/`master`); 229-290 `resolveDeliveryBranch`.
- `packages/core/src/policy/base-branch.ts` 18 `FIELD_BASE_BRANCH`; 63-141 `resolveBaseBranch` (typed `baseBranch`, else dest; invalid typed value returns `branch: ""` with an error).
- `packages/core/src/session/git.ts` 12 `GitRunner` (`(projectRoot, args) => { code, stdout }`), a different shape from `NoSuiteGitFn` (`(args, cwd) => { status, stdout, stderr }`).

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- D1. Branch. `prepareNoSuiteRun` resolves the base branch with `resolveBaseBranch(projectRoot, runGit)`, where `runGit` adapts the `NoSuiteGitFn` seam to `GitRunner`, so tests stay offline. A resolver error on a present typed value (empty `branch`) exits 2 before any fetch, with the resolver's message; no gate runs.
- D2. Remote default when nothing local names it. When the delivery branch resolves only to the framework fallback (`resolveDeliveryBranch` source `default-fallback`: no `origin/HEAD`, no remote-tracking or local `main`/`master`) and no typed `baseBranch` is set, prep asks `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` and takes the branch from the `ref: refs/heads/<b>` line (checked with `isSafeBranchName`); if that fails, it keeps `master`.
- D3. Fetch. Prep fetches with `trackingFetchArgv("origin", branch)` in place of the constant. When the head's open PR has a different base ref, that ref is fetched the same way (the existing second fetch). The no-PR merge-base fallback is the resolved branch, not `"master"`. The header names the branches fetched and where the branch came from (`plan.policy.baseBranch`, `plan.policy.deliveryBranch`, origin HEAD, or the fallback).
- D4. Missing branch. When a fetch fails, prep runs `git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin <branch>` (locale-independent, unlike matching git's stderr). Exit 2 (no such branch) gives: "check --no-suite: origin has no branch <b> (from <source>); no gate ran. Set plan.policy.baseBranch to the branch pull requests merge into, then run again." Any other result keeps today's network text.
- D5. `NO_SUITE_MASTER_REFSPEC` is removed from `no-suite.ts` and `check/index.ts`; the module doc says step 1 fetches the resolved branch.
- D6. Tests (offline, through the seams): a main-default repo (`origin/HEAD` names `main`): fetch argv names `main`, merge base against `origin/main`, header names `main`; a typed `baseBranch`; the `ls-remote --symref` fallback; a missing branch: the message names the branch and the policy key and not the network; a network failure keeps the network text; this repo's `master` case unchanged; an invalid typed `baseBranch` exits 2 before any fetch.
- D7. Scope. No other `master` literal on this path (`no-suite.ts` 30, 250-253, 260-261, 272 are all of them). One PR: `no-suite.ts`, `no-suite.test.ts`, `check/index.ts`, one `changelog.d/` fragment.

Questions for the critic:
1. Which branch should the gate fetch and merge-base against: `resolveBaseBranch` (integration branch, else delivery branch) or `resolveDeliveryBranch`? When typed `baseBranch` and `deliveryBranch` differ, should prep fetch both, given that some gates read `origin/<deliveryBranch>`?
2. Is D2 (`ls-remote --symref origin HEAD`) worth carrying, or is the resolver's local chain enough? Is it safe to run before the first fetch?
3. Is `ls-remote --exit-code --heads` the right missing-branch test, or is there a cheaper locale-safe signal from the failed fetch itself?
4. Should the missing-branch remediation name `plan.policy.baseBranch`, `plan.policy.deliveryBranch`, or the one the branch came from?
5. Remove the exported constant (D5), or keep it for callers outside this repo?
6. Does this fit one PR for the next build?

## In plain English

Given a repo whose `origin/HEAD` names `main` and no typed branch policy, when `check --no-suite` runs with no open PR, then it fetches `refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, computes the merge base against `origin/main`, never fetches `master`, and the header names `main`.

Given typed `plan.policy.baseBranch` `develop` and typed `plan.policy.deliveryBranch` `main`, when `check --no-suite` runs with no open PR, then it fetches both `develop` and `main` and computes the merge base against `origin/develop`.
Given one open PR whose base is `release`, when `check --no-suite` runs, then it fetches `release` and the delivery branch, and the merge base is against `origin/release`.

Given no `origin/HEAD`, no `main`/`master` ref and no `origin/trunk` ref, and origin's HEAD branch is `trunk`, when `check --no-suite` runs, then it fetches `trunk` before running `git remote set-head origin trunk`, resolves the delivery branch to `trunk` afterwards, computes the merge base against `origin/trunk`, and never fetches `master`.
Given the same repo but `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` fails, then prep does not run `set-head` and goes on with the fallback branch.

Given the fetch of `main` fails and `git ls-remote --exit-code origin refs/heads/main` exits 2, then the command exits 2, runs no gate, and the message names `main`, its source, and the matching policy key or fix, and does not mention network access.
Given the fetch fails and the probe exits 0, then the message keeps git's stderr and does not mention network access.
Given the fetch fails and the probe fails for another reason, then the message is today's network text.
Given `plan.policy.baseBranch` is `42`, `""`, or `bad:ref`, or `plan.policy.deliveryBranch` is `bad:ref` with no `baseBranch`, then the command exits 2 before any fetch and names the key.
Given this repo (`origin/HEAD` names `master`), then it fetches only `master` as today.
